title: The Transfer
logline: Jan tells Michael corporate decides at the end of the month and that Jim has applied for a transfer to Stamford; Pam hears it from Dwight, and Michael, still a vault, tries to talk Jim out of it without saying why.
outline: A: Michael learns the closing decision is weeks away and that Jim applied to Stamford; he tries to keep Jim without breaking his promise, admits to the office he's scared, and faxes Jan Oscar's report. B: Pam learns about Jim's transfer from Dwight and confronts him. C: Accounting, led by Oscar, builds a one-page case that Scranton is the better branch, with help from Kevin's math and Angela's clip art. Order: cold, A, B, A, C, B, A, C, B, A, B, tag
storySoFar: Jan told Michael corporate will decide at the end of the month whether Scranton or Stamford closes, and that Jim applied for a transfer to Stamford. Pam heard it from Dwight (who reads every fax), confronted Jim in the kitchen ('When?'), then told him Stamford would be good for him; neither said what they meant. Michael nearly broke his promise to keep Jim's love for Pam secret. In a short, honest meeting he told the office he can't promise anything and is scared too. Oscar, Kevin (who caught a real math mistake) and Angela (who added a cat) made a one-page case that Scranton is better; Michael faxed it to Jan with 'These are my people.' Dwight is measuring Jim's desk. Earlier: Michael secretly bought Pam's watercolor of the building; Roy set the wedding for June 10; Oscar noticed Dwight and Angela's matching bobbleheads; Kelly and Ryan are 'not not' dating.

stateChanges.progress: Jim applied to Stamford; Pam heard it from Dwight and is hurt; neither says what they mean
Decision at month's end; Michael admitted he's scared and faxed Jan Oscar's report with 'These are my people.'

stateChanges.status: Strained: she found out about his Stamford application from Dwight
Honest with each other about being scared; still secret

scenes.recap: Dwight drills the office on looking busy in case corporate visits without warning.

beats.text: Corporate inspection drill. When I say 'Jan,' everyone looks busy. Jan!

beats.caption: types furiously on a keyboard that isn't plugged in
holds a blank sheet of paper very seriously

beats.text: Stanley. You didn't move.
This is how I look busy.

scenes.recap: Jan calls: corporate decides at the end of the month, and Jim Halpert has applied for a transfer to Stamford.

beats.caption: answers the phone, sitting very still

beats.text: End of the month. Okay. And either way, you'll call me first. Before the fax.
Jim applied? To Stamford? When? No. No, I didn't know. Why would I know?
Jan. Can I say something not as a manager? I'm scared.

lines: Jan said she was scared too. Then she said, 'Don't tell anyone I said that.'
We have a lot of things we don't tell anyone. It's kind of our thing.

scenes.recap: Dwight gleefully tells Pam that Jim has applied to Stamford; she didn't know.

beats.text: Pam. Wonderful news. Jim has applied for a transfer to Stamford. I saw the fax. I read every fax.
Jim's... leaving?
Hopefully. I've already measured his desk for the Loyalty Task Force headquarters.

lines: It's a good opportunity. Stamford is bigger. It makes sense.
I just thought I'd hear it from Jim. Not from... the fax guy.

scenes.recap: Michael calls Jim in and tries to talk him out of Stamford without breaking his promise, and nearly breaks it.

beats.text: Jim. Stamford. Is this about... the thing? The vault thing?
It's a good job, Michael. It's a step up.
Because if this is about a certain person with a certain date in June—
Michael.
Vault. Vault. I said nothing. That was a hypothetical June.

lines: If Scranton closes, I need a plan. If it doesn't close... I still might need a plan.
Watching someone plan a wedding from twenty feet away is a lot. It's just a lot.

scenes.recap: Oscar decides accounting will build a one-page case proving Scranton is the better branch.

beats.text: If corporate decides on numbers, we give them better numbers. Revenue per employee. Customer retention. One page.
I'll format it. Nobody formats like me.
I'll do the math.
Kevin, you can... check the math.

lines: I don't love it here. But I'm not moving to Connecticut, and I'm not losing to Josh.

scenes.recap: Pam confronts Jim in the kitchen about hearing the news from Dwight.

beats.text: You applied to Stamford. Dwight told me. Dwight.
I didn't tell Dwight. He reads the faxes.
Were you going to tell me?
Yes.
When?

scenes.recap: Michael tells the office the decision comes at the end of the month and admits he's scared; for once, nobody makes fun of him.

beats.text: Corporate decides at the end of the month. Us or Stamford. I don't know which.
I promised you nobody would lose their job. I shouldn't have. I don't know that. I'm scared too.
Thank you for not making a speech, Michael.
I had one. It was eleven pages. It had a song.
We know you're trying, Michael.

lines: I've worked here eight years. That's the first meeting that ended early.
I don't know what to do with my afternoon.

scenes.recap: Kevin finds a real mistake in Oscar's numbers; Angela adds cat clip art; the page is done.

beats.text: Oscar. You carried the one wrong. Here. Scranton's even better than you said.
...He's right. Kevin is right. Nobody move.
I added a border. And a small cat. For professionalism.
Take out the cat.
The cat stays.

scenes.recap: Pam tells Jim, carefully, that Stamford would be good for him; neither says what they mean.

beats.text: Stamford would be good for you. Really. You're wasted here.
Yeah. Maybe.
Who's going to help me with Dwight, though?
You don't need help with Dwight. You've got the crickets.

lines: I'm happy for him. I'm happy. That's what this is.

scenes.recap: Michael faxes accounting's one-page case to Jan, with a handwritten note: 'These are my people.'

beats.caption: hands Michael a single page with a small cat in the corner

beats.text: Oscar. You did this? For us?
For me. Mostly. A little for us.

beats.caption: writes 'These are my people. - Michael' at the bottom and feeds it into the fax

scenes.recap: At five, Roy picks Pam up; she looks back at Jim, who sits in his car and doesn't start it.

beats.text: Ready? Mom wants to talk napkins tonight.
Napkins. Yeah.

beats.caption: Pam looks back. Jim doesn't start his car.

scenes.recap: Dwight starts measuring Jim's desk for his headquarters while Jim is still sitting at it.

beats.caption: measures Jim's desk with a tape measure while Jim is at it

beats.text: I'm still here, Dwight.
For now. Lift your elbow. I need the full depth.
